comment: Written against Codex CLI 2026 (Rust/ratatui TUI) from documented UI text, then re-verified against live Codex CLI 0.162.0 sessions on 2026-10-09 (Homebrew cask, alternate screen, driven through an OpenAI-compatible LM Studio provider with approval_policy on-request): every recorded screen classified correctly without a rule change. The live approval dialog reads 'Would you like to run the following command?', '› 1. Yes, proceed (y)', '3. No, and tell Codex what to do differently (esc)' and 'Press enter to confirm or esc to cancel'; the working line reads '◦ Working (3s • esc to interrupt)'; the composer reads '› Ask Codex to do anything'. Must be re-verified when Codex changes its TUI. The command/patch approval dialog ('Allow command?', 'Yes (y)', '[y/n]'), the trust-directory prompt and the 'press enter to confirm or esc to cancel' forms are BLOCKED; the '• Working (…s • esc to interrupt)' status line is WORKING; the '›' composer with its '⏎ send' footer is IDLE. The composer stays visible while Codex works, so the idle rule vetoes on 'esc to interrupt' and has the lowest priority; the approval rule vetoes on it too and anchors its patterns, because command output echoed in the transcript ('Continue? [y/n] n') must not read as an approval dialog. No rule depends on the alternate-screen flag.

anyLineRegex: (?i)press enter to confirm or esc to cancel
(?i)Do you trust the contents of this directory
